acceptedClaims.statement:
This is an attributed, independently audited port of the consecutive accepted
Yukon artifacts `upper-dependence-balance` and `upper-entropy-nogo`.  They form
one dependency-complete structural result: the first derives a necessary
condition from every deterministic private-message code, and the second proves
that a specified entropy-only relaxation of that condition cannot improve the
classical UV value.

### Finite-block code-induced balance

Let (A) and (B) be independent uniform private messages, encoded
deterministically over (n) uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast
channel.  Receiver (Y) estimates (A) with average error (p_1), and
receiver (Z) estimates (B) with error (p_2).  Define

\[
F_j=h_2(p_j)+p_j\log_2(N_j-1),\qquad \delta_j=F_j/n.
\]

For

\[
S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n),
\]

the exact telescope is

\[
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[I(A;B\mid S_i,Y_i)-I(A;B\mid S_i,Z_i)\right]
=I(A;B\mid Y^n)-I(A;B\mid Z^n).
\]

Both endpoints are nonnegative, while Fano bounds them by (F_1) and
(F_2), respectively.  With independent uniform time (T), and

\[
U=A,\quad V=B,\quad W=S_T,\quad X=X_T,\quad Y=Y_T,\quad Z=Z_T,
\]

every such code therefore induces

\[
\left|I(U;V\mid W,T,Y)-I(U;V\mid W,T,Z)\right|
\le\max\{\delta_1,\delta_2\}.
\]

The complete induced law retains the fixed coordinate map:

\[
p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=\frac1n p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w\mid u,v,t)
\mathbf 1\{x=f_t(u,v)\}P_{YZ\mid X}(y,z\mid x).
\]

In particular, (U\perp V), (T\perp(U,V)), (X=f_T(U,V)), and the
realized state (W) cannot select another encoder map after (u,v,t) are
fixed.  The same variables satisfy four compatible rate rows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_1&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+\delta_1,\\
R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+I(X;Z\mid U,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+I(X;Y\mid V,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2.
\end{aligned}
\]

This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition.  The alphabets of the
messages and (W) grow with blocklength, so it is not by itself a fixed-
cardinality single-letter outer region.

### Exact entropy/copy no-go theorem

At uniform input, put

\[
h=h_2(1/4),\qquad c=h-1/2,\qquad r=h-3/4.
\]

Consider the coarse entropy relaxation that imposes:

- the complete seven nonempty entropies of the common-noise BSSC coupling,
  namely (H(X)=1), (H(Y)=H(Z)=h),
  (H(X,Y)=H(X,Z)=H(Y,Z)=3/2), and (H(X,Y,Z)=2);
- message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map equality,
  the memoryless Markov equality, and exact dependence balance;
- every conditional BEC identity
  (I(L;Y,Z\mid K)=\tfrac12I(L;X\mid K)) for disjoint subtuples
  (L,K\subseteq\{U,V,W,T\}), with (L\ne\varnothing);
- the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side
  (r).

There is an actual finite entropic point satisfying all these constraints for
which both direct sum branches equal

\[
\boxed{2h_2(1/4)-\frac54
=0.3725562489182657\ldots}.
\]

Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable
information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot
lower this relaxation below that value.  Nor can any finite sequence of
standard copy-lemma extensions: each copy step can be realized by conditional
resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and
objective.

The witness is deliberately not a binary BSSC distribution.  Its (X) is a
tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.  Exact binary-
posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude it and
remain viable.  The theorem obstructs only the stated entropy/copy refinement
route.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The audit establishes both components of the claim. For every deterministic finite-block private-message code, the conditional-mutual-information sum telescopes exactly, Fano bounds its endpoints, time sharing yields the stated approximate dependence balance, memorylessness and deterministic encoding give the fixed-coordinate induced-law factorization, and chain-rule/Csiszar identities prove all four rate rows. For the specified entropy-only BSSC relaxation, the sharp scalar support inequalities are verified and an actual finite entropic witness satisfies the complete listed constraints while attaining both sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. Because the witness is genuinely entropic, universally valid finite-variable information inequalities cannot remove it; conditional resampling preserves it through every finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions.

The no-go conclusion applies only to the stated coarse entropy/copy relaxation and finite sequences of standard copy-lemma extensions.
The finite witness is deliberately not a binary-input BSSC law: X is tuple-valued. Exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints can exclude it and remain viable.
The theorem does not establish a new capacity upper bound.

value.title: Finite-block code-induced dependence balance and compatible rate rows
value.summary:
This is the finite-block component of an attributed, independently audited port of the consecutive accepted Yukon artifacts `upper-dependence-balance` and `upper-entropy-nogo`, which together form one dependency-complete structural result. Let A and B be independent uniform private messages of sizes N₁,N₂≥2, encoded deterministically over n uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channel. Receiver Y estimates A with average error p₁ and receiver Z estimates B with average error p₂. Define Fⱼ=h₂(pⱼ)+pⱼ log₂(Nⱼ−1), δⱼ=Fⱼ/n, and Sᵢ=(Yⁱ⁻¹,Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ). Then exactly

Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ [I(A;B∣Sᵢ,Yᵢ)−I(A;B∣Sᵢ,Zᵢ)] = I(A;B∣Yⁿ)−I(A;B∣Zⁿ).

Both endpoints are nonnegative, while Fano bounds them by F₁ and F₂, respectively. With independent uniform time T and U=A, V=B, W=S_T, X=X_T, Y=Y_T, Z=Z_T, every such code induces

|I(U;V∣W,T,Y)−I(U;V∣W,T,Z)| ≤ max{δ₁,δ₂}.

The complete induced law retains the fixed coordinate map:

p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=(1/n)p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w∣u,v,t) 1{x=f_t(u,v)}P_{YZ∣X}(y,z∣x).

In particular, U⊥V, T⊥(U,V), X=f_T(U,V), and realized W cannot select another encoder map after (u,v,t) are fixed. With Rⱼ=(1/n)log₂Nⱼ, the same variables satisfy

R₁≤I(U,W;Y∣T)+δ₁,
R₂≤I(V,W;Z∣T)+δ₂,
R₁+R₂≤I(U,W;Y∣T)+I(X;Z∣U,W,T)+δ₁+δ₂,
R₁+R₂≤I(V,W;Z∣T)+I(X;Y∣V,W,T)+δ₁+δ₂.

This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition. The message alphabets and W may grow with blocklength, so it is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region and does not establish a new capacity upper bound.

value.title: Exact entropy/copy no-go theorem for the stated coarse BSSC relaxation
value.summary:
At uniform input, put h=h₂(1/4), c=h−1/2, and r=h−3/4. Consider the coarse entropy relaxation imposing: (i) the complete seven nonempty entropies of the common-noise BSSC coupling, namely H(X)=1, H(Y)=H(Z)=h, H(X,Y)=H(X,Z)=H(Y,Z)=3/2, and H(X,Y,Z)=2; (ii) message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map equality, the memoryless Markov equality, and exact dependence balance; (iii) every conditional BEC identity I(L;Y,Z∣K)=(1/2)I(L;X∣K) for disjoint subtuples L,K⊆{U,V,W,T}, L nonempty; and (iv) the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side r. There is an actual finite entropic point satisfying all these constraints for which both direct sum branches equal

2h₂(1/4)−5/4 = 0.3725562489182657… .

Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot lower this relaxation below that value. Nor can any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions: each copy step can be realized by conditional resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and objective. The witness is deliberately not a binary BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components. Exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude it and remain viable. The theorem obstructs only the stated coarse entropy/copy relaxation and finite sequences of standard copy-lemma extensions; it does not establish a new capacity upper bound.

value.title: Telescope, Fano, fixed-map factorization, and conditioned Csiszár proof
value.summary: Set Dᵢ=I(A;B∣Yⁱ,Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ) for 0≤i≤n. The ith balance summand is exactly Dᵢ−Dᵢ₋₁, so summation gives the claimed endpoint telescope without a channel inequality. Separate Fano bounds control D_n by F₁ and D₀ by F₂. After uniform time sharing, memorylessness and deterministic encoding give the fixed-coordinate induced-law factorization because, conditional on (A,B,T), the current input is fixed and the current output is independent of the past/future outputs in W. The individual rate rows follow from Fano and forward or reverse chain rules. The two sum-rate rows follow from conditioned Csiszár sum identities; the uncancelled remainders are respectively ΣᵢI(Yⁱ⁻¹;Yᵢ) and ΣᵢI(Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ;Zᵢ), hence nonnegative.

value.title: Posterior-support calculation and finite entropic counterfeit construction
value.summary: For g(q)=I_Z(q)−I_Y(q), direct differentiation gives g″(q)=(2q−1)/(ln(2)q(1−q)(1+q)(2−q)), so g is concave through 1/2 and convex thereafter. The exact identities g(1/5)=(8/5)r and g′(1/5)=−2r make 2r(1−q) a global upper support. A posterior mixture of mass 5/8 at 1/5 and 3/8 at 1 has mean 1/2 and support value r; reflection gives the other direction. The finite witness uses mutually independent binary components C,A,B1c,B2c,Eu,Ev,Ny,Nz with respective entropies 2r, 1−h, r, 7/4−2h, 1/2−r, r, 1/2, 1/2, and tuple variables U=(C,A,B2c,Eu), V=(B1c,Ev), X=(C,A,B1c,B2c,Eu,Ev), Y=(C,A,Ny), Z=(C,B1c,B2c,Nz), with W,T constant. Component-set intersections verify the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, all conditional BEC identities, exact dependence balance, both support rows, and both objective branches. Because this is an actual finite distribution, every universally valid finite-variable information inequality holds. Conditional resampling realizes each finite standard copy-lemma extension while preserving the original marginal and objective.

value.title: Exact affine-in-h entropy-witness checker
value.summary: A reproducible standard-library Python checker represents every component entropy as an exact rational affine expression a+bh with h=h₂(1/4). Using weighted component unions and intersections rather than floating-point arithmetic, it checks positivity from 3/4<h<7/8, the complete base entropy vector and structural equalities, both zero-valued dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both sharp support rows, and both objective branches at 2h₂(1/4)−5/4. It reports successful exact audits for the affine-in-h construction, the 65 BEC identities, dependence balance, support rows, and both branches.

acceptedClaims.statement: For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional defined in this contribution is exactly additive under products. On a receiver-skew channel the branchwise functional equals the averaged functional, and the same equality and additivity hold for every finite product of receiver-skew channels. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every integer n >= 1, both functionals on P^{times n} equal n(2 h_2(1/4) - 5/4) bits. This is a theorem only about the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals, not about tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or the capacity itself.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The supplied proof establishes exact additivity of the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional for finite-alphabet product broadcast channels, including correlated product inputs and joint envelope auxiliaries. Receiver-skew symmetry equates the branchwise and averaged functionals and extends their additivity to finite products. Using the dependency’s BSSC inequality and contact identity, it also derives the exact half-skew BSSC value n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) for every n>=1.

The BSSC specialization relies on the declared dependency for the supporting inequality and contact identity.

value.title: Product tensorization of separately relaxed UV scalar functionals
value.summary: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W and input law p, define t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)−I_p(X;Z), let 𝔠[f](p) be the upper concave envelope of f at p, and put A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+𝔠[−t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+𝔠[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional defined in this contribution is exactly additive under products. On a receiver-skew channel the branchwise functional equals the averaged functional, and the same equality and additivity hold for every finite product of receiver-skew channels. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every integer n >= 1, both functionals on P^{times n} equal n(2 h_2(1/4) - 5/4) bits. This is a theorem only about the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals, not about tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or the capacity itself. The BSSC specialization relies on the previously accepted sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequality and contact identity.

value.title: Concave-envelope product decomposition and receiver-skew symmetrization
value.summary: For a product channel, opposite-order mutual-information expansions and the Csiszár sum identity decompose the conditional receiver-information difference into factorwise terms. Applying this to every posterior ensemble bounds the upper concave envelopes of t and −t by the sums of their factor envelopes, including for correlated product inputs and auxiliaries joint across factors. Output entropy subadditivity supplies the corresponding A and D upper bounds. Product input laws and independent products of factor posterior ensembles give the reverse inequalities, proving exact additivity of B_avg without an attainment assumption. For a receiver-skew involution S, relabeling gives A(Sp)=D(p) and D(Sp)=A(p); concavity at (p+Sp)/2 then proves B_br=B_avg and permits restriction to invariant input laws. Product involutions extend this equality and additivity to finite products. For the half-skew BSSC, the invariant binary input is uniform, and the previously accepted sharp posterior-support inequality together with its attaining posterior mixture evaluates both envelopes there as h_2(1/4)−3/4, yielding n(2h_2(1/4)−5/4).

value.title: High-precision half-skew BSSC relaxed-UV specialization checker
value.summary: A reproducible standard-library Python script evaluates the BSSC mutual-information formulas at 90-decimal precision, checks the support contact at q=4/5, the attaining posterior mixture with masses 5/8 and 3/8, the receiver-skew channel relations, and the normalized value 2h_2(1/4)−5/4. It corroborates the exact BSSC specialization; the universal product and symmetry theorem rests on the analytic proof.

value.title: Proof of the conditional 30-row specialization, marginalization, and restricted-value consequences
value.summary: Starting from the explicitly assumed encoded Theorem 9 premise, set R0=0, expand the displayed minima into 26 scalar rows, and split the two interval side conditions into four nonnegative-slack rows. Exact comparison with the independently generated local path rows establishes the stated 30-row specialization. The exhaustive output-term audit shows that every information term contains only one auxiliary group and one receiver output; consequently, replacing an admitted joint auxiliary-receiver law by the product of its input-only G and K marginals preserves each required marginal and every row. The premise's quantifier order then gives the stated infimum bound without interchanging the receiver infimum and input-prior supremum. Restricted feasible-set inclusion gives V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K). For Q0-supported hierarchies, the endpoint receiver-information functions vanish, so the posterior identities reduce every audited row to the four midpoint values (c,g,k,c). The explicit zero-rate hierarchy and binary-output individual-rate bounds establish the claimed finiteness on the realizable (g,k)-domain.

value.title: Structured-premise row expansion and exhaustive single-output term audit
value.summary: The accepted claim is established using two exact constructions of the private-message constraint system: direct expansion of the structured equations (19a)-(19p) and side conditions, and independent generation from generic three-link path formulas. Rows are compared after only the chain-rule normalizations I(U,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(U;A|W) and I(V,W;A)=I(W;A)+I(V;A|W). value.title: Proof of finite-grid reduction, exact Q0 infima, and coercive midpoint bounds
value.summary: The proof first applies the posterior-measure sampled-curve method to replace each finite-output receiver by an at-most-N-output receiver while preserving all receiver terms in the accepted 30-row system on Q; reflection of posterior measures preserves an already reflected pair when Q is reflection closed. On Q0, each auxiliary block is parameterized by three nonnegative quantities (A,U,V), and every row depends on the four receivers only through (c,g,k,c). Three explicit feasible witness families H, L, and X cover the high, low, and straddling cases and establish V_0(g,k) >= max{F(g),F(k)}. A reflection-invariant three-output revealing-erasure receiver with midpoint value c, together with the SL(1,U) row when all four sampled curves agree, gives both Q0 infima at c. Solving F(g),F(k) <= U on their two scalar branches yields the stated necessary midpoint window. The argument remains conditional on the accepted 30-row foundation and makes no continuum or unconditional converse claim.

value.title: Posterior-measure sampled-curve reduction for finite grids
value.summary: Represent a finite-output binary-input receiver under the fair prior by a finite posterior measure of mean 1/2 and express its mutual-information curve J_A(q) as an integral of the sampled posterior kernel. For an N-point grid containing 0, 1/2, and 1, apply Caratheodory's convex-hull theorem to the posterior coordinate and the N−2 nonendpoint curve samples, obtaining at most N posterior atoms with the same mean and all the same samples on Q. Posterior-conditioning identities express every receiver term in the accepted 30-row audit through these samples, so the replacement preserves the restricted optimization exactly. Reflection is handled by pushing the posterior measure forward under rho -> 1-rho, which preserves an already reflected pair on a reflection-closed grid. This method is only a fixed-finite-grid reduction and supplies no continuum receiver-cardinality theorem.
